memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milkah, who was the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor. The woman was very beautiful, a virgin; no man had ever slept with her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar and came up again." - Gen 24:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a detail — before the servant had even finished praying, Rebekah was already walking to the well. God's answer was on its way before the request was complete. She was from Abraham's own extended family, exactly the sort of woman he had prayed about.

This tells us something wonderful about God. He is not slow or distracted. He was already at work arranging the answer while the servant's words were still forming. The Bible says our Father knows what we need before we ask (Matt 6:8), and sometimes He sets the answer in motion long before we see it.

You may be praying today about something that feels far off. Take heart. God is not waiting to begin only when you finish. He is already moving people, opening doors, and lining up circumstances you cannot see. Rebekah did not know she was an answer to prayer as she went about her ordinary chores — and often God uses ordinary, faithful people who have no idea how they fit into His plan.

Keep praying, and keep your eyes open. The answer may already be walking toward the well.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God is already at work before I finish praying?
2. Where might I be part of God's answer to someone else's prayer?
3. How does God's foreknowledge encourage me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are already at work before I even finish asking. Help me to trust Your timing and to keep my eyes open to Your answers. Amen.
